result.title: Grounded Credit Assignment in Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Turn Search Agents
result.summary: Outcome-reward reinforcement learning such as GRPO gives every token of a search-agent rollout the same advantage, although the rollout exercises two capabilities: finding evidence and using it. We show that accuracy improves without grounding: Search-R1 raises accuracy on all seven QA benchmarks, yet on Bamboogle the evidence-supported share of correct answers falls from 84.0% to 42.9%. We attribute this to GRPO's credit assignment: rollouts that retrieve answer-bearing evidence are favoured in aggregate only in proportion to their accuracy gain over the rest, a grounding gap that answering from memory or misusing evidence shrinks or reverses. To address this, we propose Grounded Credit Assignment (GCA), which uses verifiable sub-outcomes (evidence retrieval and answer correctness) to correct search and answer credit separately: a wrong answer is blamed more than the search that found the evidence, and a correct answer that bypasses retrievable evidence is credited less. Never negative on evidence-finding search, the correction does not shrink with the grounding gap; capped at 10% of each token's advantage, it never overrides the outcome signal. Without extra models, rollouts, or training stages, GCA improves average EM over Search-R1 by 5.7 (Qwen2.5-3B) and 6.3 points (Qwen3-30B-A3B) and raises this share from 76.9% to 93.4%.

AI.brief_summary: 论文诊断多轮搜索智能体的信用分配问题：GRPO 把「找到证据」与「使用证据」混在同一优势里，导致准确率上升但「有证据支持的正确回答」占比从 84.0% 降至 42.9%；为此提出 GCA，用可验证子结果分别修正检索与回答的信用。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「答案是否真正依赖检索证据」的旁路诊断与子结果信用修正机制（限幅、不覆盖结果信号），可能为 LVR 中视觉旁路检测与 latent 内容贡献分配的训练监督提供可核查线索；但对象是纯文本搜索智能体，迁移需人工判断。
